modules.title: Power Apps capabilities and app building
modules.summary: Compares app types and walks through basic canvas and model-driven app building.

lessons.title: Power Apps capabilities and use cases
lessons.summary: Compare canvas apps, model-driven apps, plans, code apps, Power Pages context, and Copilot-assisted creation.
learningObjectives: Compare canvas, model-driven, Power Pages, and code app options
Identify when screen layout control makes a canvas app a good fit
Explain how plans and Copilot can accelerate app creation
Choose the right Power Apps approach for a business scenario
lessons.explanation: Power Apps offers several build paths. Canvas apps give makers direct control over screens, controls, and Power Fx formulas. Model-driven apps are driven by Dataverse tables, forms, views, and relationships. Plans in Power Apps can draft broader solutions from natural language. Code apps let developers create custom web apps on the managed platform. Power Pages is the related Power Platform choice for external websites. Copilot can accelerate creation, but makers still review generated design and security.

terminology.definition: Dataverse-driven app with forms and views.
Developer-built web app on Power Platform.

lessons.businessScenario: Adventure Works needs three experiences: warehouse staff need a phone checklist, supervisors need a structured request-management workspace, and suppliers need an external status site.
lessons.technicalExample: Choose a canvas app for the barcode checklist, a model-driven app over Dataverse for supervisor case work, Plans to draft the first solution outline from the business description, and Power Pages for the supplier-facing website.

misconception.myth: Canvas apps are always the advanced choice because they offer more layout control.
misconception.reality: Model-driven apps are often the better and faster choice when Dataverse tables, relationships, forms, and views should define a consistent process UI.

lessons.examTakeaway: Read for the user experience clue: custom task screen means canvas, Dataverse process workspace means model-driven, natural-language solution draft means Plans, and developer-hosted web app means code app.
lessons.recap: Compare canvas apps, model-driven apps, plans, code apps, Power Pages context, and Copilot-assisted creation.
lessons.simplerExplanation: Choosing an app type is like choosing a vehicle: a bicycle is nimble for a route you design yourself, while a train works best when the tracks and stations already define the journey.
lessons.anotherExample: A bank might use a canvas app for a lobby greeter tablet, a model-driven app for relationship managers, and a code app when developers need a custom React experience under Power Platform governance.

lessons.title: Build a basic canvas app from data
lessons.summary: Create a canvas app from data and customize it with real Power Fx formulas.
learningObjectives: Describe how to create a canvas app from a data source
Identify controls, galleries, forms, and screens used in a basic canvas app
Apply Power Fx formulas to filter, display, and update data
Explain how preview and testing confirm a canvas app works
lessons.explanation: A canvas app is a custom task tool. Makers choose data, generate or design screens, then customize controls with Power Fx. Real formulas include `Filter(EquipmentRequests, Status = "Open")` for a gallery, `SubmitForm(EditForm1)` for a save button, `Navigate(scrDetails)` for navigation, and `IsBlank(txtTitle.Text)` for validation. Copilot can suggest apps and formulas, but makers test permissions, delegation, accessibility, and business fit. Practise this in the Dataverse table and canvas app lab.

terminology.definition: Control for viewing or editing a row.
Connection to data such as Dataverse or SharePoint.

lessons.businessScenario: Tailwind Traders technicians open a phone app each morning to see only their open equipment requests, update photos and notes, and submit the repair status before leaving the site.
lessons.technicalExample: Set the request gallery Items property to `SortByColumns(Filter(EquipmentRequests, AssignedTo.Email = User().Email && Status = "Open"), "CreatedOn", SortOrder.Descending)`. Use `SubmitForm(EditForm1)` on Save and show a warning label when `IsBlank(txtResolution.Text)`.

misconception.myth: Generated canvas apps are finished as soon as Power Apps creates the browse, detail, and edit screens.
misconception.reality: Generated screens are a starting point; makers still refine formulas, accessibility, delegation, validation, sharing, and the task flow.

lessons.examTakeaway: For canvas build questions, look for data source selection, generated screens, control properties, Power Fx formulas, save/publish/share steps, and data permissions.
lessons.recap: Create a canvas app from data and customize it with real Power Fx formulas.
lessons.simplerExplanation: A canvas app is a customizable field clipboard: you decide which boxes appear, which list is filtered, and what the Save button does when the technician taps it.
lessons.anotherExample: A nonprofit check-in app could use `LookUp(VolunteerShifts, Code = txtCode.Text)` to find a shift, then `Patch` or a form submit to record arrival time.

lessons.title: Build a basic model-driven app
lessons.summary: Build from Dataverse tables, forms, views, app designer pages, publishing, and roles.
learningObjectives: Describe how Dataverse tables, forms, and views shape model-driven apps
Identify app designer pages and navigation used to assemble the app
Explain why publishing and security roles are needed before sharing
Order the steps to build and share a basic model-driven app
lessons.explanation: A model-driven app starts with Dataverse. Model tables and relationships, configure forms and views, create app pages in the app designer, validate, publish, and share with appropriate security roles. This approach is strong for data-dense processes with consistent navigation and responsive experiences. AI can draft model-driven components, but makers validate names, columns, forms, views, relationships, roles, and ALM. Practise this in the model-driven app for equipment requests lab.

terminology.definition: Defines how a row is viewed or edited.
Filtered and sorted list of rows.
Tool to compose app pages and navigation.

lessons.businessScenario: Contoso dispatch supervisors need a command center for equipment requests where related departments, tasks, notes, and status history are easy to navigate without designing every screen from scratch.
lessons.technicalExample: Create Equipment Request, Department, and Request Task tables; configure a main request form with tabs for assignment and resolution; create Open Requests and High Priority views; add the tables as pages in app designer; validate, publish, and share with dispatcher and manager security roles.

misconception.myth: Model-driven app makers mainly arrange pixels on a blank screen.
misconception.reality: Model-driven app makers spend most effort on the Dataverse model, forms, views, relationships, business rules, pages, and security roles.

lessons.examTakeaway: For model-driven build questions, start with Dataverse tables and relationships, then forms and views, then app designer pages, validation, publishing, and security roles.
lessons.recap: Build from Dataverse tables, forms, views, app designer pages, publishing, and roles.
lessons.simplerExplanation: Building a model-driven app is like designing a train station from a timetable: once the tracks, stops, and routes are defined, the passenger experience follows a consistent pattern.
lessons.anotherExample: An alumni office could build a model-driven app over Alumni, Donations, and Events tables, with views for major donors and forms for pledge follow-up.
